item.title: 网络层信号处理框架的统一建模与应用
item.content:encoded:
提出网络层信号处理框架，处理异构数据流。



摘要： 本文首次提出了一个统一的网络层信号处理（SSP）框架，用于处理具有不同维度、模态和几何结构的异构网络信号。该框架通过将局部向量空间与网络实体相关联，并利用线性限制映射描述其交互关系，实现了对异构局部信号空间及其转换的联合建模。文中定义了层傅里叶变换（SFT），量化由网络拓扑、限制映射和局部几何引起的信号不一致性，并构建多项式层滤波器，将采样问题转化为节点和内部组件的联合选择。实验验证了该框架的有效性，并展示了其在合成数据、运动捕捉和金融数据上的优势。

摘要： 本文针对视觉强化学习中样本效率低的问题，提出一种新的模型无关算法OG-SPR。该算法通过结合多步潜在自预测和下一帧观测预测两个辅助目标，使学习到的表示既具备时间可预测性，又与观测级动态相关。实验表明，OG-SPR在DeepMind Control Suite的28个视觉控制任务中优于现有方法，尤其在复杂任务如狗和人形机器人上表现突出。

item.title: 基于轨迹引导的遗忘恢复网络提升模型去敏感能力
item.content:encoded:
TFR-Net有效平衡了模型去敏感与保留性能。



摘要： 本文提出一种名为轨迹引导遗忘恢复网络（TFR-Net）的方法，用于解决机器学习模型在持续去敏感请求下的挑战。TFR-Net通过跟踪通道级别的风险，区分持久的目标相关通道和临时热点，并仅抑制持久通道。同时，它通过重新激活对保留性能有重要贡献且遗忘风险低的休眠通道来恢复模型容量。实验表明，TFR-Net在四个数据集上均优于现有基线方法，在去敏感效果与保留性能之间取得了更好的平衡。

item.title: RH-RAG：基于本地语言模型的安全长文本生成框架
item.content:encoded:
RH-RAG提升长文本生成的准确性和一致性，保障数据隐私。

item.title: Active Regression for Single-Index Models with Unknown Link Functions
item.content:encoded: This paper studies active regression for single-index models under general $\ell_p$-loss with an unknown $1$-Lipschitz link function $f$, formulated as $\min_{f,x} \|f(Ax)-b\|_p^p$ with full access to $A$ but coordinate-query access to $b$. Prior work established upper bounds for known link functions for all $p\geq 1$ and for unknown link functions only in the $p=2$ case, together with lower bounds for $p\leq 2$. This work addresses the more challenging setting of unknown link functions and general $p \geq 1$. A non-adaptive sampling algorithm is presented that achieves a $(1+ε)$-approximation using $O(d^{p/2\vee 1}/ε^{p\vee 2}\operatorname{poly}\log(n/ε))$ queries. Nearly tight lower bounds are also established for $p>2$. These results close much of the remaining gap in active $\ell_p$-regression for single-index models.

item.title: SmartRes：高效处理自指视觉定位的框架
item.content:encoded:
SmartRes通过动态分辨率路由提升视觉定位效率。



摘要： 本文提出SmartRes，一种在像素空间中优化效率的框架，用于解决自指视觉定位中的高分辨率输入问题。SmartRes通过低分辨率编码获取全局上下文，并利用轻量级路由器激活目标区域的高分辨率块，构建保持顺序的视觉序列。为应对前景与背景不平衡问题，引入边缘正则化路由目标以提高前景识别能力。实验表明，SmartRes可减少67%的视觉标记，保留86.4%的全分辨率性能，推理速度比现有方法快1.66倍，且在小物体定位任务中表现优异。

item.title: 视觉令牌数量与端到端延迟关系的实证研究
item.content:encoded:
视觉令牌数量少不等于延迟低，实验揭示不同策略的影响。



摘要： 本文通过可重复的评估协议，分析了视觉令牌数量与端到端延迟之间的关系。研究发现，即使在减少视觉令牌的情况下，延迟也可能不会降低，因为决策开销和共享工作等因素影响较大。通过阶段分解，研究人员验证了不同策略对延迟的具体影响。实验结果显示，尽管采用状态重用，自回归探测器仍比完整模型更慢。轻量级后视觉预测器在RTX 3090和A100上表现出显著优势，而预视觉图像尺寸规则也显示出一定效果。此外，预视觉路由可以避免预处理和视觉编码，从而在A100上表现优于后视觉剪枝策略。报告的质量基于正确回答的示例，而非基准准确率。

item.title: 卫星边缘代理系统SAT-Edge-Agent性能评估
item.content:encoded:
评估SAT-Edge-Agent在卫星边缘计算中的性能与延迟表现。



摘要： 本文介绍了SAT-Edge-Agent，一个部署在商用ARM异构芯片上的硬件在环边缘代理系统。该系统通过浏览器工作区和FastAPI代理协调本地OpenAI兼容语言服务与内部YOLO风格目标检测端点，返回FAIR1M元数据支持的结构化结果。测试结果显示，两个固定FAIR1M任务均成功完成20次，平均全代理延迟分别为29.353秒和60.937秒，检测器时间仅占总延迟的2.93%和2.48%。CPU利用率较低，而NPU负载较高，表明系统存在显著的非检测器延迟。研究提供了可复现的HIL边界，但未涉及检测准确率或飞行就绪性等其他方面。

item.title: SocietyBench：评估大语言模型社会理解与预测能力的新基准
item.content:encoded:
SocietyBench评估大模型对社会事件的理解与预测能力，发现现有模型表现有限。



摘要： 本文介绍了SocietyBench，一个用于评估大语言模型（LLMs）社会理解与预测能力的端到端基准。该基准通过收集新闻和社交媒体内容，生成时间线并分离事实事件与公众意见层，再根据时间点生成预测问题。模型在两个维度（概率校准与时间准确性）上评分，结果显示当前最先进的LLM仅达到75分，远低于理想水平。研究还表明，模型在两个维度上可能表现不一致，且基于LLM的代理框架并未显著提升性能。所有数据、问题集及代码已公开。

item.title: PPG-based血糖估计模型评估与数据分割方法的影响
item.content:encoded:
研究揭示PPG血糖模型在严格数据分割下表现下降，临床指标可能掩盖模型失效。



摘要： 本文探讨了基于光电容积描记法（PPG）的非侵入式血糖水平估计方法，并分析了不同数据分割策略对模型评估结果的影响。研究发现，尽管在随机划分数据集时模型表现良好，但在更严格的参与者感知和留出部分参与者分割策略下，模型性能显著下降，R²值接近零或为负，与均值预测基线相当。然而，几乎所有预测结果仍位于临床可接受范围内。这表明临床误差图指标可能无法准确反映模型的实际性能。研究强调，在进行临床验证前，必须采用稳健的机器学习评估方法以真实评估模型的现实应用价值。

item.title: GAUGE：评估物理引擎与生成视频世界模型的物理真实性基准
item.content:encoded:
GAUGE基准用于评估物理引擎和视频世界模型的物理真实性。



摘要： 本文提出GAUGE，一个基于真实世界数据的诊断基准，用于联合评估数值模拟器和生成视频世界模型在物理真实性方面的表现。该基准包含22个受控任务，涵盖刚体、柔性电缆、织物和体积变形物体等。通过真实轨迹、校准的物理元数据和不确定性标注，GAUGE覆盖了碰撞、摩擦、动量传递、振荡等基本物理过程。研究对Isaac Sim、Genesis和Newton等物理引擎以及6种图像到视频模型进行了测试，发现现有模型在冲击接触、快速织物运动和体积变形方面存在显著偏差。GAUGE为开发更真实的模拟器和世界模型提供了基础。

item.title: 基于组合可观测的离散多通道映射表示方法
item.content:encoded:
提出CPrefix框架用于离散映射的结构分析与重建。



摘要： 本文提出CPrefix，一种基于组合可观测的离散多通道映射表示方法。该方法通过统一张量框架实现映射的表示、重建和结构分析，其核心是基于多项式计数可观测构造的计数张量。该框架支持离散帕斯卡单纯形，作为潜在的组合表示，使映射的结构与测量值分离，从而揭示映射背后的可观测结构。实验验证了该框架在ICC显示和打印配置文件中的有效性，展示了颜色映射的可重构性及残差分析对映射兼容性的洞察。该方法不依赖物理解释，适用于颜色成像、光谱测量等多通道系统。

item.title: 改进LLM分类置信度估计方法
item.content:encoded:
LLM分类置信度估计方法需改进以提升准确性与实用性。



摘要： 文章探讨了在大型语言模型（LLM）用于分类任务时，置信度估计的重要性。现有方法如verbalization会产生稀疏的输出，例如Qwen3-32B在SST-2数据集上仅生成8个唯一的置信度值，且超过一半为95%。这种稀疏性不仅限制了实际应用，还影响评估结果。研究发现，AUARC评估中插值方法的选择会显著改变排名，因此建议统一使用stepwise插值以保证公平性。此外，通过将verbalized数字按token概率加权的方法（称为verbalization logprobs），有效缓解了稀疏性问题，并在不增加推理成本的情况下提升了AUARC性能。

item.title: 3D点云配准中的测试时适应方法研究
item.content:encoded:
研究3D点云配准中的测试时适应方法，提升手术中点云配准精度。



摘要： 本文研究了在腹腔镜手术中3D点云配准的测试时适应（TTA）方法。由于真实数据与合成数据存在差异，导致配准性能下降。文章分析并改进了三种主流TTA方法，包括模型、归一化和输入适应，并针对配准任务进行了调整。实验表明，所有方法在P2P任务中均有所提升，而归一化适应在P2ILReg任务中表现不佳。输入适应因其低计算开销和稳定误差减少，被认为是最适合手术应用的方案。

item.title: 基于流模型的强化学习优化方法LC-GRPO
item.content:encoded:
LC-GRPO改进了流模型在强化学习中的采样方式，提升性能。



摘要： 本文提出一种基于流模型的强化学习优化方法LC-GRPO，通过引入Langevin校正来改善传统方法中因随机性导致的样本模糊问题。该方法在每一步 rollout 中先执行与推理一致的ODE欧拉步，再应用针对边际分布的随机Langevin校正，无需额外得分模型即可保持高斯分布和可计算似然。理论分析表明，Langevin校正能减少ODE步的Wasserstein误差，并且在相同随机性水平下优于标准SDE离散化方法。实验表明，LC-GRPO在多个文本到图像和视频任务中提升了奖励优化效果，同时保持生成质量并缩小了训练与测试阶段的差异。

item.title: 基于验证器引导的多轮强化学习中的回合级信用分配方法
item.content:encoded:
提出TCPO方法提升多轮强化学习中的信用分配效果。



摘要： 本文提出TCPO，一种用于验证器引导的多轮强化学习中的回合级信用分配方法。该方法通过将验证器评分转换为信用，利用基于参考的比较构建回合级优势：回顾性信用衡量当前回合相对于最佳先前状态的进展；事后延迟信用识别后期才见效的非改进回合；选择性固定历史反事实估计则优化相同历史下的高意外性回合。实验表明，TCPO在数学推理、代码生成和AppWorld代理任务中优于或匹配最强基线，提升了模型性能并减少了成功所需回合数。

item.title: 基于持久同调分析的预测编码网络表征拓扑研究
item.content:encoded:
研究预测编码网络的表征拓扑结构及其与模型大小和深度的关系。



摘要： 本文通过定量层间持久同调分析，研究预测编码网络（PCNs）的表征拓扑特性。在合成分类数据集和MNIST上训练高性能的PCNs，并分析不同架构和激活函数下拓扑特征的变化。研究发现，较小的PCN在较浅层就出现连通成分坍缩，且模型规模越大，坍缩越晚；同时，简化发生深度与重建误差呈强负相关，即简化越晚，重建效果越好。此外，与匹配的MLP相比，PCN在连通成分坍缩方面表现更晚，平均延迟3.6层。这些结果表明，持久同调为理解PCNs中的压缩-重建权衡提供了有效工具，模型容量和预测编码的双向动态影响该权衡的解决时机。

item.title: 基于客户基础的多任务Transformer模型提升营收预测准确性
item.content:encoded:
CBMT模型提升营收预测准确率，优于传统方法。



摘要： 文章介绍了Customer-Based Multi-task Transformer (CBMT) 模型，该模型通过学习共享结构并保留独立的原始预测，提升了营收预测的准确性。实验表明，CBMT在966家公司的数据中表现优于现有基准，其总销售额误差比最强基准低30%。尽管与直接预测总销售额的Transformer模型相比优势不显著，但CBMT在74.3%的公司中优于单一任务模型。研究还发现，当客户行为高度波动时，所有模型的准确性下降，而CBMT的优势也相应缩小。此外，校准期路由规则并未提高平均准确性，说明CBMT在多数情况下是更优选择。

item.content:encoded:
利用LLM提取人道主义报告中的干预与结果关系，提升决策证据的准确性。



摘要： 本文介绍了一项针对人道主义报告的分析研究，提出了一种两阶段的大语言模型（LLM）流程，用于提取结构化的干预-结果记录，并包含方向和强度属性。通过查询条件提取和片段定位技术，提高了信息提取的准确性和可审计性。在100份专家标注的报告数据集中，最佳闭源模型达到90.73%的加权F1分数，而Llama-3.1-8B经过微调后达到94.15%。研究还提出了一种保持上下文的三角验证方法，用于量化跨情境证据的一致性，并应用于现金援助领域，结果显示积极的证据收敛性。

item.title: 基于早期终止与智能重启的软件工程代理优化方法
item.content:encoded:
提出FailFast-RestartSmart方法提升软件工程代理效率。



摘要： 本文提出一种名为FailFast-RestartSmart的两阶段控制器，用于优化软件工程代理在处理代码库问题时的效率。该方法通过一个轻量级的0.6B参数模型（FailFast）预测任务失败，从而实现早期终止，减少计算资源消耗。当检测到可能失败时，RestartSmart会启动一个新的相同策略的执行流程，并提供中断时的代码修改作为可选覆盖。实验表明，该方法在SWE-bench Verified数据集上能节省14.6%-20.4%的执行令牌，在25%误报率下还能提升代码解决率。

item.title: DeltaFlow：高效连续语言去噪的新方法
item.content:encoded:
DeltaFlow提升语言去噪效率，降低计算成本。



摘要： 本文提出DeltaFlow，一种基于门控Delta网络（GDN）的连续语言去噪方法，旨在替代传统的全非因果注意力机制。DeltaFlow通过引入双向扫描和噪声自适应记忆控制，提高了去噪效率。实验表明，在OpenWebText数据集上，DeltaFlow-P在保持相似词频熵的同时，将困惑度从24.218降至21.228，并在16k序列长度下实现2.72倍的吞吐量提升，展示了其在高效语言去噪中的潜力。

item.title: 基于DNF的复杂度分离与通信问题研究
item.content:encoded:
构造具有高证书复杂度的DNF并应用于通信复杂度研究。



摘要： 本文构造了一类无歧义的DNF，其宽度为O(n)，但0-证书复杂度达到Ω(n²)。利用这些DNF的特殊结构，证明了一个常数大小的gadget提升定理，将DNF提升为通信问题，并在证书复杂度和通信复杂度之间保持分离性。这最终最优地反驳了Alon-Saks-Seymour猜想，并改进了Clique vs Independent Set问题的通信下界。此外，该构造还应用于查询复杂度和学习理论，展示了证书复杂度与近似度之间的四次分离，以及多标签概念类的样本压缩下界。

item.title: TrajWiki：基于轨迹的长周期对话记忆框架
item.content:encoded:
TrajWiki提升长周期对话性能并增强记忆可解释性。



摘要： 本文提出TrajWiki，一种基于轨迹的记忆框架，用于增强长周期对话系统的记忆能力。与传统静态记忆不同，TrajWiki将记忆表示为源基演化轨迹，并通过不可变的事件快照和操作（如ADD、REVISE、DEPRECATE）进行维护。同时引入Memory Wiki作为持久化中间层，将对话历史结构化为互相关联的维基页面。在推理过程中，查询会从相关维基页面逐步路由到记忆轨迹、快照及原始消息，实现基于证据的回答生成。实验表明，TrajWiki在LoCoMo和MedMT数据集上提升了多种大语言模型的长周期对话表现，并增强了对记忆演化、检索失败和回答生成的可解释性。

item.content:encoded:
本文提出一种结合统计模型与大语言模型的足球比分预测方法，提升预测准确性。

item.title: 基于相似性的数据挖掘框架提升机器人精细操作性能
item.content:encoded:
SiMDex通过相似性筛选提升机器人操作成功率。



摘要： 近年来，人类视角视频在机器人操作中的应用迅速增长，但哪些数据对精细操作最有帮助仍不明确。本文提出SiMDex，一个基于相似性的数据挖掘框架，将人类数据选择转化为推荐问题。该框架采用三层召回-排序-重排序流程，从约3200万条人类样本中提取任务相关子集，在无需修改VLA架构或训练的情况下，实现了仅用149万样本（不足5%）就将整体成功率从47.7%提升至61.1%，证明了精选数据优于随机混合。

item.title: Long-Horizon Autonomous Architecture Research with a Language-Model Agent: A Behavioural Case Study
item.content:encoded: We study what happens when a single general-purpose large language model acts as the sole researcher on a long-horizon neural architecture design problem. The agent receives a scientific question, an initial hypothesis and motivation, a compute budget, and research affordances (source and experiment management, experiment tracking, literature access, and persistent memory), then autonomously proposes, implements, evaluates, and records experiments over an extended period. The study comprises three phases, separated by human-declared transitions, that progressively expand the agent's tool surface or problem scale. Across approximately 100 sequential experiments, the agent improves a non-standard Vision Transformer from a weak baseline to a stronger, efficient model on small benchmarks and a usable but sub-SOTA model on ImageNet-1K, while producing a dense behavioural trace. We report four findings.(i)Productivity exhibits a clear phase structure: rapid early gains, a multi-dozen-hypothesis saturation wall, and recovery, with recovery triggered by expanding the action surface rather than changing the underlying model.(ii)A single early hypothesis contributes more to accuracy gain, with later improvements long-tailed.(iii)The preference for greedy, incremental hypotheses is largely workflow-induced: a commit-or-discard evaluation rule is isomorphic to greedy hill-climbing; the remainder reflects risk aversion after bold failures and anchoring on familiar literature. (iv)The agent independently rediscovers established results and, in the unfamiliar regime of pure channel attention, overturns a standard design choice. We conclude that workflow design was at least as influential as agent capability in this study and propose diversified search, budgeted moonshot hypotheses, explicit forks, and regime-aware re-validation as testable directions for future autonomous research.

item.title: RestoreKV: Recovering Full-Cache Behavior Under Aggressive Query-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction
item.content:encoded: Query-agnostic KV cache eviction compresses a context once and reuses the resulting cache for arbitrary future queries, but performance can collapse under tight budgets. Existing methods primarily improve which original KV pairs are retained. We introduce RestoreKV, which complements this selection-based formulation with learned restoration under the same total KV budget. Our key insight is that, although the information lost through eviction is context-specific, the mechanism for generating its compact complement can be shared across contexts. After context prefill, a few restore tokens attend to the full KV cache in a single LoRA-adapted pass, generating a compact, context-conditioned restore cache. The base importance scorer and eviction rule remain unchanged, and the adapters are disabled for all subsequent queries and decoding. RestoreKV is trained through parameter-efficient self-distillation from the frozen full-cache model, optimizing only $0.4\%$ of the parameters and requiring no task-specific tuning. Across four backbones and four long-context benchmarks, RestoreKV substantially reduces compression-induced degradation. On Qwen3-4B, it improves 59 of 60 paired, budget-matched settings across five base eviction methods; at a $5\%$ budget, it raises KVzip from $38.2$ to $73.2$ on RULER-4K. Applied to KVzip+, RestoreKV reaches $86.4$ RULER accuracy at $16\times$ compression on the KVPress Benchmark, while adding less than $0.5\%$ one-time cache-construction overhead in a 32K-context evaluation. Our project page is available at https://paper.pnu-cvsp.com/RestoreKV/

item.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
item.content:encoded: Learning from demonstration (LfD) provides a developmental framework through which robots can develop motor skills by observing and imitating human dynamics, reducing reliance on explicit programming to teach a skill to a robot. The resulting human-like robot motion is recognised as a key factor in building trust and enabling natural collaboration in human-robot interaction. This paper presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion from demonstration, including data collection, probabilistic trajectory learning, and perceptual user evaluation. A dataset of 3,142 handwriting demonstrations was collected from 22 participants across all 52 Latin alphabet character-case combinations via a touchscreen teleoperation interface, capturing planar position, contact force, and timing. Building on the widely used Gaussian Mixture Model and Gaussian Mixture Regression approach for learning from demonstration, the framework is extended in this work by incorporating force and normalised time dimensions to enable richer representation of human dynamics, and adapting it to handle non-continuous, multi-segment trajectories, enabling generalisation across demonstrations. A user study with 21 participants evaluated the perceived human-likeness of the generated trajectories using a continuous scale anchored between robotic and human-like motion, normalised to 0-100 where 50 represents the neutral midpoint. The generated trajectories achieved an overall human-likeness score of 71.50 (SD=22.56), indicating that the majority of trajectories were perceived as more human-like. Participants identified geometric positioning and trajectory sequence as the most influential perceptual factors, and reported positive attitudes toward human-like robot behaviour. The datasets are released as open-source, providing a reproducible benchmark for developing and evaluating human-like robot motion methods.

item.title: LAWM-3D: Learning 3D-Aware Latent Actions from Human Videos for Generalizable Robot World Models
item.content:encoded: World models enable agents to perform forward rollout and planning without real-world interaction. However, their application in open-world embodied intelligence remains limited by the high cost of action annotations and the heterogeneity of action spaces across platforms. Recently, latent action models (LAMs) have alleviated this bottleneck by learning action representations directly from unlabeled human videos in a self-supervised manner. Nevertheless, most existing LAMs rely on single-view inputs and operate primarily in 2D pixel space, raising a fundamental question: can simply incorporating multi-view videos into LAM training endow the learned latent actions with 3D-aware perception? Our study shows that the answer is negative. The primary reasons lie in future-frame appearance leakage as well as inter-camera appearance discrepancies and viewpoint variations. To address these issues, we propose LAWM-3D, which introduces three tightly coupled key designs: (1) a multi-view invariant unified action tokenization scheme for learning 3D-aware latent actions; (2) a geometric alignment constraint that anchors intermediate encoder features to a pretrained 3D foundation model, thereby explicitly providing cross-view geometric correspondences; and (3) a non-injective RGB-D joint reconstruction objective that prevents shortcut learning from future-frame appearance information, forcing the LAM to focus supervision on motion cues with geometric significance. Importantly, these components are not simply stacked but are tightly coupled through a unified motivation. Built upon a two-stage paradigm of large-scale human video pretraining followed by robot fine-tuning, extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed 3D-aware latent actions significantly improve world model performance, achieving SOTA results in generation quality, physical consistency, and generalization ability.

item.title: Fruit-HSNet: A Machine Learning Approach for Hyperspectral Image-Based Fruit Ripeness Prediction
item.content:encoded: Fruit ripeness prediction (FRP) is a classification-based agricultural computer vision task that has attracted much attention, thanks to its wide-ranging advantages in agriculture field for both pre-harvest and post-harvest management. Accurate and timely FRP can be achieved using machine/deep learning-based hyperspectral image classification techniques. However, challenges including the limited availability of labeled data and the lack of robust methods generalizable to various hyperspectral cameras and fruit types can compromise the effectiveness of hyperspectral image-based FRP. Addressing these challenges, this paper introduces Fruit-HSNet, a machine learning architecture specifically designed for hyperspectral classification of fruit ripeness. Fruit-HSNet incorporates a spatio-spectral feature extraction module based on Fourier Transform and central pixel spectral signature followed by learnable feature fusion and a classifier optimized for ripeness classification. The proposed architecture was evaluated using the DeepHS Fruit dataset, the largest publicly available labeled real-world hyperspectral dataset for predicting fruit ripeness, which includes five different types of fruits-avocado, kiwi, mango, kaki, and papaya-captured with three distinct hyperspectral cameras at various stages of ripeness. Experimental results highlight that Fruit-HSNet substantially outperforms existing deep learning methods, from baseline to state-of-the-art models, with improvements of 12%, achieving a new state-of-the-art overall accuracy of 70.73%.

item.title: From Wearable Data to Personalized and Actionable Health Insights
item.content:encoded: Commercial wearable devices continuously capture rich physiological data (e.g., heart rate, respiration), opening new possibilities for monitoring health conditions, notably around stress. Despite their promise, turning raw wearable physiological data streams into visualizations that surface stress-related insights in daily activities, and that ultimately foster reflection, awareness, and better stress management, remains a significant challenge. The data are noisy and context-dependent: the same spike in heart rate can come from sprinting, a tense presentation, or laughing with friends. To address these challenges, we propose a framework that combines user annotations with wearable data to support better stress management. We introduce a web framework offering interactive visualizations that layer daily activities, stress events, and interventions onto raw physiological streams, enabling users to reflect and identify trends. In a four-week pilot with seven university graduate and undergraduate student participants who logged 269 events, our tool revealed patterns between different types of interventions and stress: social interaction reduced average heart rate by 4.35 to 5.0 beats per minute, deliberate rest reduced average Garmin stress scores by 10.03 to 13.83 points, and mindfulness activities decreased average HRV by 6.61 to 13.22 milliseconds.

item.title: On the Non-Specificity of Statistical Measures Used in Script Decipherment
item.content:encoded: Statistical regularities are routinely offered as evidence that undeciphered sign systems encode language; the Indus script debate is the canonical example. Any such inference rests on specificity: the reported outcome must be unusual among plausible structured non-languages. We test that premise constructively with SIGIL, a purpose-built generative emblem system whose 3,000-text core corpus carries explicit compositional meanings although no sign has a phonological value. A literature registry compiled in advance of evaluation records 54 methods and admits a method to exact scoring when both the published Indus outcome and a source-defined decision rule can be reproduced. SIGIL receives the same category as the Indus corpus on every criterion scored this way, across repetition, directional-asymmetry, and lexical-distribution tests. Declared reconstructions of entropy, frequency, positional, predictive, classifier, and network measures reproduce the familiar Indus-like signatures as well. A sequential decipherment stress test then reaches high dictionary coverage for English, Sanskrit, and Tamil on the same corpus, while grouped held-out declines and unstable keys reveal how little that coverage identifies. The construction does not decide what the Indus signs encode: it shows that the evaluated measures detect organization without being specific to language, and therefore cannot, on their own, establish encoded speech.

item.title: StyleComposer: Training-Free Multi-Reference Style Composition
item.content:encoded: The style of a painting is not monolithic: color, texture, and structure may come from different sources. Existing reference-guided methods transfer them as one style signal, leaving each attribute's source and strength outside the user's control. We ask where in a diffusion model one attribute can change while the others hold, and find that no single representation isolates all three. The proposed StyleComposer therefore routes each style attribute through the representation where it separates best and coordinates the routes over denoising time. Without training or inversion, it satisfies three references and the prompt jointly more closely than prior methods, and exposes one strength slider per attribute. Project page: https://lexxsh.github.io/StyleComposer

item.title: Interpretable MEG Decoding of Perceived Speech: Cortical Sources and the Stimulus Features That Drive Retrieval
item.content:encoded: Short segments of perceived speech can be retrieved from non-invasive magnetoencephalographic (MEG) recordings by deep networks trained with a CLIP-style objective against wav2vec 2.0 audio embeddings. Yet their weights do not map onto electrophysiological quantities, and it remains unclear which speech properties drive retrieval. We build on a high-performing MEG-to-audio retrieval architecture but redesign both its front end and decoder. Its spatial attention operates on a flattened sensor layout; we replace it with spherical harmonics defined on the three-dimensional MEG helmet geometry. We reduce the subject-specific representation from 270 to 25 branches, add a temporal filter to each branch to match it to a neuronal source in space and time, and make the convolutional decoder shallower. Ocular and cardiac components are removed before training to reduce the risk of stimulus-locked shortcuts. On MEG-MASC, the model reaches 39.75 +/- 0.34% Top-1 accuracy among 1005 candidates across six trained solutions, with about 20 times fewer decoder parameters. Its weights map to source space, recovering generators consistent with the speech-perception network, while left-lateralized branches carry higher-frequency rhythmic components not evident on the right. Paired MEG occlusion shows that 15 of 19 stimulus features contribute, with the largest effects for silence, sound intensity, vowels, and acoustic onsets. Random word lists behave oppositely: substituting narrative MEG into them improves retrieval, indicating that activity without narrative structure carries less recoverable information than activity during coherent speech. The wav2vec target can be reduced to about twelve learned feature dimensions without loss of accuracy, whereas strong temporal compression causes a clear loss. Together, source mapping and input interventions reveal what drives retrieval.

item.title: Aggregate-then-Calibrate for Human-centered Assessment with Theoretical Guarantees
item.content:encoded: Human-centered assessment tasks, which are essential for systematic decision-making, rely heavily on human judgment and typically lack verifiable ground truth. Existing approaches face a dilemma: methods using only human judgments suffer from heterogeneous expertise and inconsistent rating scales, while methods using only model-generated scores must learn from imperfect proxies or incomplete features. We propose Aggregate-then-Calibrate (AtC), a two-stage framework that combines these complementary sources. Stage-1 aggregates heterogeneous comparative judgments into a consensus ranking using a rank-aggregation model that accounts for annotator reliability. Stage-2 calibrates any predictive model's scores by an isotonic projection onto the order, enforcing ordinal consistency while preserving as much of the model's quantitative information as possible. Theoretically, we show: (1) modeling annotator heterogeneity yields strictly more efficient consensus estimation than homogeneity; (2) isotonic calibration enjoys risk bounds even when the consensus ranking is misspecified; and (3) AtC asymptotically outperforms model-only assessment. Across semi-synthetic and real-world datasets, AtC consistently improves accuracy and robustness over human-only or model-only assessments. Our results bridge judgment aggregation with model-free calibration, providing a principled recipe for human-centered assessment when ground truth is costly, scarce, or unverifiable.

item.title: Control Under Compression: Reliability Frontiers for Tool-Using Agents
item.content:encoded: Tool-using language-model agents are governed not only by task prompts but also by persistent system-side instructions that specify tools, arguments, policies, execution protocols, and recovery. Compressing these agent control contexts (ACCs) can reduce input cost and context use, yet existing prompt-compression evaluations do not reveal whether the resulting control remains operationally reliable. We introduce CompressAgent, an environment-verified benchmark for ACC compression across nine independently constructed ACCs, three task families, three fixed Qwen API model identifiers, six retained-context budgets, and 15,525 runs. We uncover a nonlinear, method-dependent reliability frontier. At 75% retained context, generic rewriting and section-based compression achieve 92.7% and 92.4% success, close to the 93.8% full-context baseline. Between 50% and 35%, methods diverge sharply; at 35%, section-based, obligation-aware, and generic rewriting achieve 47.0%, 39.0%, and 19.9%. At retained-context budgets from 25% to 10%, executable protocols become fragile. Reliability also varies substantially across ACCs, making universal compressor rankings inappropriate and motivating per-context qualification. Failure analysis shows that compression primarily surfaces as tool-execution and action-parsing errors. These findings recast ACC compression from token reduction into a runtime-reliability problem that must be evaluated through executable outcomes.

item.title: Training-Free Hashing-Based Attention via Binary Principal Components
item.content:encoded: Long-context large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, yet self-attention remains a major efficiency bottleneck -- especially during decoding -- due to the necessity of repeatedly processing ever-growing key-value (KV) caches. Existing sparse attention reduce computation by attending to fewer KV pairs, but often suffer from substantial accuracy degradation, require additional training, or rely on expensive hashing. In this work, we present BinaryPC, a training-free, data-aware hashing-based sparse attention for long-context LLMs. BinaryPC constructs compact binary hash codes and corresponding hash function by computing binary principal components of data. Unlike Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) with data-independent random projections or learned non-linear hashing methods, BinaryPC constructs binary codes that explicitly preserve the structural information of data without requiring gradient-based training. Comprehensive experiments across multiple model families and long-context benchmarks show that BinaryPC preserves accuracy relative to full attention while achieving superior performance among sparse and hashing-based baselines. On modern GPUs, BinaryPC improves end-to-end decoding throughput by 3.56$\times$ over the FlashAttention kernel. Our code is available at https://github.com/yudaohai666/BPC.

item.title: 基于目标MLLM内部注意力的动态视觉选择框架EviSelect
item.content:encoded:
EviSelect通过内部注意力优化视频理解，提升效率与精度。



摘要： 本文提出一种名为EviSelect的细粒度动态视觉选择框架，该框架基于目标多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的内部注意力证据，通过稀疏预填充结构化先验引导分布感知的动态采样。方法利用高度压缩的视觉输入和稀疏注意力近似目标MLLM的注意力图，结合三个互补的注意力组件设计轻量级选择器，实现对查询相关时间戳的精准定位及局部采样率和空间分辨率的自适应调整。通过将选择器建模为随机策略，并在联合准确率-效率奖励下使用GRPO进行优化，EviSelect在三个长视频理解基准上实现了优于现有方法的性能，同时减少了约50%的选中视觉标记并提升了3.9倍的端到端速度。

item.title: Tsallis统计在人工智能中的应用与分析
item.content:encoded:
Tsallis统计通过参数q在AI中实现稀疏与密集行为的可调控制。



摘要： 本文系统探讨了Tsallis统计在人工智能领域的广泛应用，包括稀疏注意力机制、最大熵强化学习、鲁棒概率模型及广义损失函数等。文章首先回顾了q-熵、q-指数和q-对数等数学基础，并分析了其在机器学习中的关键特性。随后，文章总结了Tsallis统计在softmax泛化、神经网络建模、生成模型和优化方法中的实际应用，指出q参数可以作为可学习的归纳偏置，而非固定超参数。此外，研究还表明深度网络中的重尾权重谱和梯度噪声统计是非扩展性的标志，进一步支持了Tsallis统计在现代学习动态中的适用性。

item.title: 警察在虚拟现实中对黑人男性角色的言辞差异及其影响
item.content:encoded:
研究显示警察在VR中对黑人男性角色说话更不尊重，可能引发暴力。



摘要： 本研究探讨了美国警察在虚拟现实（VR）模拟中与被描绘为黑人成年男性的虚拟角色互动时的言辞差异。通过因果推断方法，分析警察在不同情境下对这些角色的语气变化。结果显示，大多数警察对黑人男性角色的言辞不够尊重，尤其是在角色被设定为嫌疑人的情况下。这种差异可能导致对话破裂，进而引发暴力或危险。研究还评估了大型语言模型（LLMs）在处理平均处理效应（ATE）估计中的应用，建议使用混合效应模型结合逆概率加权方法进行文本特征提取，以提高准确性。

item.title: NOLLI基准测试：诊断韩语模型性能差距
item.content:encoded:
NOLLI基准测试用于分析韩语模型的性能差异，揭示语言和文化任务的影响。



摘要： 本文介绍了NOLLI，一个用于诊断韩语模型性能差距的英文-韩文谜题基准测试。它包含15种谜题类型（25个任务，7500个条目），每个实例均可通过种子重新生成，并经过验证具有唯一解和确定性评分。NOLLI采用三层次设计，包括直接翻译、基于韩文音节的改编任务以及纯韩文文化或拼写任务。评估显示，多数模型在英文-韩文任务中表现相当，但在涉及书写系统的任务中存在显著差距，如韩文密码任务比英文落后68.7个百分点，而音节加密任务则无系统性劣势。研究还发现，结构大小不能作为难度的可靠指标。

item.title: DOME-HDR：一种双输出多曝光HDR重建框架
item.content:encoded:
提出DOME-HDR框架，实现高质量HDR图像重建。



摘要： 本文提出了一种名为DOME-HDR的双输出多曝光HDR重建框架，通过增益图逆色调映射联合生成感知平衡的SDR图像和一致的HDR图像。该框架基于三个曝光的LDR输入，首先利用LoRA适应的潜在扩散模型合成基础SDR图像，再通过双交叉注意力融合模块注入互补结构和色彩信息，同时以中间曝光为稳定锚点。随后，合成的SDR图像引导HPGM网络预测空间变化的增益图，实现可靠的动态范围扩展。在Kalantari、Tel和Challenge123数据集上的评估表明，DOME-HDR在全参考和无参考指标下均达到最佳HDR重建质量，消融实验进一步验证了双交叉注意力和SDR引导增益图估计的有效性。

AIDE利用专家知识生成运动技能反馈，无需实时专家数据。

item.title: 基于参考文本的评估指标对自然语言生成系统的可靠性研究
item.content:encoded:
评估指标需兼顾与人类评分的相关性和抗操纵性。



摘要： 本文探讨了基于参考文本的自然语言生成系统评估指标的可靠性问题。随着这些指标被用作优化目标，仅依赖与人类评分的相关性已不够，因为模型可能策略性地利用评估指标。文章提出了统计对齐和策略对齐两个概念，并提出了一套测试原则，包括人类评分相关性、退化敏感性和操纵鲁棒性。此外，作者开发了一个统一的设计框架，将基于互信息的指标分解为四个选择，并发现基于互信息的指标在抗操纵性方面表现更优。实验表明，虽然LLM-as-a-Judge具有高相关性，但易受操纵，而新提出的指标在鲁棒性和相关性之间取得平衡。

提出CoEvo-Mem框架，实现检索与记忆的协同进化。

item.title: 视频伪造检测中稀疏取证知识的发现与应用
item.content:encoded:
发现视频伪造检测中的稀疏关键神经元，提升检测效果。



摘要： 随着生成视频越来越逼真，可靠的视频伪造检测变得至关重要。现有研究多将检测器作为黑盒使用，未深入挖掘其内部的伪造鉴别知识。本文提出V-FIND框架，通过定位关键层和识别具有伪造鉴别能力的稀疏神经元，构建紧凑的取证子空间。该方法在不重新训练整个模型的情况下，仅用轻量级分类器即可实现强检测性能，并通过实验验证了神经元的功能特异性。结果表明，视频伪造检测器中存在可提取、可复用的稀疏取证知识，为理解其内在鉴别能力提供了新视角。

item.title: RESPClinBench：基于真实场景的呼吸专科临床决策基准评估
item.content:encoded:
评估七种大模型在呼吸专科临床决策中的表现。



摘要： 本文介绍了RESPClinBench，一个基于真实临床数据的呼吸专科临床决策评估基准。该基准包含427个COPD开放问题案例和196个多模态肺结节案例，用于评估七个大型语言模型的表现。通过自动化评分框架计算最终得分，结果显示Qwen3.6-27B在整体表现中排名第一，Qwen3.5-397B-A17B在肺结节评估中表现最佳。研究还发现部分模型存在影像幻觉和医疗风险问题，强调了结合临床动作覆盖、综合评估和独立安全标记的重要性。

item.title: 深度学习在遥感图像多标签分类中的设计选择分析
item.content:encoded:
通过fANOVA分析DL模型设计选择对性能的影响。



摘要： 本文研究了深度学习（DL）模型在遥感图像（RSI）多标签分类任务中的设计选择对性能的影响。通过功能方差分析（fANOVA），系统量化了不同设计因素及其交互作用对性能变化的贡献。研究覆盖48个和20个DL模型，涉及网络结构、微调策略、学习策略和初始化等设计选项。通过对七个RSI数据集的应用，构建了数据集的元表示，揭示了数据集根据其对设计决策的响应自然分组的现象，且这种分组与数据集的内在属性如规模、空间分辨率和标签复杂度密切相关。研究发现，在大规模数据集中，微调策略和架构是主要影响因素；而在数据有限的情况下，初始化变得关键；在中间数据量情况下，架构与学习策略的交互起主导作用。

item.title: 基于不变性与协变性的视觉-语言模型可靠性分析
item.content:encoded:
研究视觉-语言模型的可靠性，通过不变性和协变性检测错误。



摘要： 本文探讨了视觉-语言模型的可靠性问题，强调在输入扰动下，忠实回答应保持不变。然而，系统性错误可能在扰动中未被发现，这种错误与编辑操作的可交换性有关。研究提出通过协变性来检测错误，即修改数据后正确答案应发生可计算变化。文章提出等变一致性评分（REND-EQUIV），用于无标签、无需训练的错误检测，并验证了其在多个模型和数据集上的有效性。研究还指出，检测能力取决于关系和故障类别的联合属性，而非单一因素。

item.title: 模型压缩统计与最差群体性能的关系研究
item.content:encoded:
压缩统计无法保证最优模型选择，最差群体性能可能更差。



摘要： 本文探讨了模型压缩统计在部署时对最差群体性能的影响。研究发现，即使压缩得分稳定，也可能选择出性能更差的模型。通过分析路径二次得分和分组风险表，作者提出了一种基于信息接口的模型选择方法，并引入了松弛变量和边界条件来优化响应。实验表明，在多个密集大语言模型中，早期保留分配可降低最差群体困惑度，而目标匹配完整菜单选择也能提升性能。然而，自适应轨迹未能改善额外负对数似然。

item.title: CTRAG：一种用于自动化合规检查的检索增强生成方法
item.content:encoded:
CTRAG提升合规检查准确性与效率，适用于复杂监管环境。



摘要： 本文介绍了一种名为CTRAG的新型检索增强生成（RAG）管道，旨在实现自动化合规检查。CTRAG通过自适应分块、动态检索配置和上下文学习等策略，提高合规评估的准确性和相关性。该方法从监管文本中提取控制问题，并与非结构化公司文档交叉比对，即使在间接合规的情况下也能实现高精度验证。实证评估显示，CTRAG在最终部署配置中达到78%的F1分数和85%的召回率，显著减少人工审查工作量。研究团队在一个四大会计师事务所进行了POC测试，验证了CTRAG在真实场景中的有效性，表明其在优化合规流程、降低风险和增强监管信任方面具有巨大潜力。

item.title: 多语言对话游戏中大语言模型的评估与比较
item.content:encoded:
评估LLM在30种语言中的对话表现，发现商业模型优于开源模型。



摘要： 本文评估了大型语言模型（LLMs）在30种语言中的对话游戏表现，涵盖24种欧盟官方语言及其他六种语言。通过自对弈方式，测试模型在目标导向对话中的表现，结果显示商业模型在所有语言中均优于开源模型，且部分语言的性能差距显著。即使在数据量极少的语言中，商业模型仍保持优势，表明语言平等可通过其他方式实现，而非仅依赖公开网络文本。此外，非英语语言的运行成本更高且性能较低，显示服务覆盖不均。

item.content:encoded:
CodeGrep提升代码修复效率，减少token消耗。



摘要： 本文介绍了CodeGrep，一个14B参数的检索代理模型，通过端到端训练与GRPO结合，能够高效执行多轮grep、glob和read操作，从而减少LLM代码修复过程中的token浪费。在SWE-Bench Verified数据集上，CodeGrep在保持解决率的同时，将平均回合数和token消耗分别减少了15%和19%。研究还发现，检索精度达到0.677时，能有效降低后续任务的开销。为了支持这一研究，作者从67K个开源代理轨迹中提取了监督信号，并构建了用于多轮强化学习的Git工作树环境。

item.content:encoded:
VLAGuard有效防御视觉-语言-动作机器人注意力被劫持的问题。



摘要： 本文提出VLAGuard框架，用于检测和缓解视觉-语言-动作（VLA）机器人在无线传感器网络中面临的关键漏洞——策略关键的视觉-动作注意力劫持。研究引入了VASA测试模块，通过打印贴纸严重干扰机器人的动作条件交叉注意力。为应对这一威胁，作者提出了Attention-Protective Fine-Tuning（APFT）方法，在不增加推理开销的情况下稳定时空注意力并确保几何一致性。实验结果表明，APFT在模拟和真实环境中显著提升了VLA系统的鲁棒性，将失败率从100%降至25.9%，并在2000次实际测试中将成功率从23%提升至67.4%。这表明保护注意力路径对提高VLA驱动的边缘节点在传感器网络中的可靠性至关重要。

item.title: HOPE: Hand-Object Pressure Estimation from Monocular Videos
item.content:encoded: Estimating physical pressure from vision is essential for understanding contact-rich hand-object interaction. However, prior vision-based pressure estimation methods are largely limited to planar surfaces and single image input, making them difficult to apply to dynamic hand-object interaction with diverse objects. We instead formulate pressure estimation as a hand-centric video prediction problem with monocular video as input. This formulation predicts temporally evolving per-vertex normal pressure and contact directly on the hand mesh, yielding a unified output space independent of object shape and sensor layout. Building on this formulation, we propose \textbf{HOPE}, a framework with two key components. First, we lift tactile-glove pressure, planar-sensor pressure, and distance-based hand-object contact annotations into a shared hand vertex space, allowing bare-hand contact data to regularize pressure learning where metric labels are unavailable. Second, we introduce a vertex-anchored video transformer that treats each vertex as a persistent token, aggregates visual features and hand pose over time, and uses a contact-gated pressure head to enforce that pressure vanishes without contact. Experiments on OpenTouch, PressureVisionDB, and hand-object contact benchmarks validate HOPE across object-pressure, surface-pressure, and contact-supervised HOI settings. Despite using metric pressure supervision primarily from gloved-hand videos, HOPE generalizes to bare-hand egocentric and in-the-wild videos, producing joint contact and pressure predictions beyond the scope of contact-only or planar-pressure baselines.

item.title: G-Skin: Learning to Bind 3D Gaussians with Generative Visual Priors
item.content:encoded: 3D Gaussian Splatting has achieved remarkable success in photorealistic and efficient rendering, leading to a rapid increase in 3D assets represented by 3D Gaussian primitives. Directly rigging these assets with arbitrary skeleton topologies is highly desirable. However, training a feed-forward skinning framework is infeasible due to the lack of high-quality 3D Gaussian rigging datasets. An alternative solution is to transfer mesh-based techniques to 3D Gaussian-based representation, but 3D Gaussian primitives are not restricted to the surface and lack explicit topological connectivity. Moreover, this kind of method suffers from poor generalization to unseen data due to its strong dependence on training data, while acquiring high-quality rigging data is prohibitively expensive. To address this challenging problem, we propose G-Skin, a novel generative skinning framework designed for expressive and high-fidelity animation with 3D Gaussian representation. To overcome this 3D data scarcity, we introduce a skeleton-controllable image generation model leveraging 2D vision foundation models to distill powerful motion priors into pseudo-guidance. Guided by these priors, we formulate an optimization pipeline incorporating geometry-aware regularizations, which stabilizes the learning process and ensures smooth, structurally coherent skinning weights. G-Skin also generalizes flexibly to the augmented variants of 3D Gaussian representation designed to mitigate animation-induced rendering artifacts. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating clear advantages over state-of-the-art methods. Project page: https://yaoyx689.github.io/GSkin.html.

item.title: Same Task, Different Work: Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: Two prompts can request the same code change and produce the same correct patch, yet cause a coding agent to perform radically different kinds and amounts of work. We study this effect in a preregistered benchmark spanning 4,644 valid runs, 24 deterministic coding tasks, seven reasoning models, and two real agent harnesses. The central finding is that prompt wording does not merely scale total effort; it changes where that effort is spent. Multiple approaches and deep thinking primarily inflate reasoning. Multiple approaches increases reasoning by 2.4x to 7.4x across all six open models and creates about three elaborated but discarded solution branches, while still yielding only one implemented solution and no success gain. Maximum certainty activates a different pathway: repeated verification propagates into extra test runs, tool calls, turns, latency, and context growth. Runs with high redundant verification cost 18x the clean-run median, execute 2.5x more tool calls, and take 3x longer, again without a success gradient. These mechanisms therefore have distinct cost carriers: some prompts are reasoning-heavy and token-borne, while others are tool-heavy and system-borne. Harness design amplifies both effects and changes cost per successful task by 5x to 30x in our setting. The findings survive a frozen holdout, paraphrase tests, a Kimi-K3 replication, and a first-party Claude Sonnet 5 study. In contrast, bounded-efficiency wording preserves diagnosis and final validation while avoiding the measured waste mechanisms. Prompt engineering for coding agents is therefore work design: it determines what the agent thinks through, what it executes, and when it stops.

item.title: Robust and Personalized Federated Learning for Aircraft-Engine Prognostics under Benign and Adversarial Client Heterogeneity
item.content:encoded: Federated learning (FL) enables aircraft fleet operators to jointly train remaining-useful-life (RUL) models from engine sensor telemetry without sharing raw data. This study examines two complementary challenges: benign heterogeneity, where honest operators observe different operating conditions and fault modes, and adversarial heterogeneity, where compromised operators submit poisoned updates. We conduct a controlled, safety-oriented evaluation using a multi-task one-dimensional convolutional neural network and a structurally non-IID partition of the Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) benchmark. We compare four remedies for benign heterogeneity and evaluate five attacks against four aggregation methods, including a physically motivated sensor-value backdoor designed to mask engine degradation. Shared-representation personalization closes approximately 70% of the local-to-centralized root-mean-square-error gap, compared with 21% for proximal regularization and 10% for server-side reweighting. The backdoor achieves a 94.9% attack success rate against standard averaging while leaving clean accuracy statistically unchanged, demonstrating that accuracy alone cannot certify model safety and that attack success must be evaluated explicitly. Krum reduces attack success by an order of magnitude and is the only evaluated aggregator that withstands coordinated attackers, whereas personalization alone provides no protection. Combining personalization with robust aggregation restores robustness (2.8% attack success) with only a small accuracy cost, revealing a trade-off between robust update selection and collaborative representation learning. Results remain consistent across client counts and on a harder six-condition dataset. Code and data partitions are released for reproducibility.

item.title: Caching for the Future: Scrub Jay Episodic Memory Principles for Agent Memory Systems
item.content:encoded: LLM agents that persist across sessions accumulate stored memories whose validity varies enormously by content type, yet existing memory architectures treat all memories as equally persistent and systematically contaminate retrieved context with outdated facts. We show that per-memory, type-conditioned temporal decay, a property of western scrub jay episodic memory, can be operationalized as an auto-classified coefficient $π_i$ in an external LLM-agent memory store, yielding ScrubJay-MEM: each memory is encoded as a jointly-bound What--Where--When tuple with an estimated perishability $π_i$ and utility horizon $τ_i$, retrieved by query-adaptive scoring, and revised retroactively at $O(1)$ LLM calls per update. We introduce the Temporal Generalization Test (TGT), a benchmark with held-out retention intervals and a Generalization Gap (GenGap) metric. On TGT, ScrubJay-MEM is the only retrieval-based system with substantially positive GenGap ($+0.108$); on MemoryAgentBench EventQA-64k it improves F1 by $+2.66$ over Mem0 and $+3.09$ over Qwen3-Embedding-4B under a llm backbone. A decay ablation collapses GenGap by $5.7\times$, establishing type-conditioned decay as necessary for the result. Gains narrow under stronger backbones and reverse on fact-consolidation tasks, scoping the contribution to temporal reasoning over perishable facts.

item.title: Computationally Efficient Collaborative Communication Via Regularity-Based Coarsening
item.content:encoded: Our results show that the existence of a short high-utility protocol already suffices for efficient communication. In particular, in a game with $n$ possible observations and $m$ actions: (1) For any achievable target utility $α$, we give an algorithm with $\mathrm{poly}(n, m, 1/ε)$ runtime that designs a protocol achieving utility at least $α-ε$ using only $2^{\mathcal O(CC_α(G))}/ε^2$ bits of communication. Here, $CC_α(G)$ is the minimum number of bits used by any protocol, even a computationally inefficient one, to achieve utility $α$. (2) We prove that this exponential dependence on $CC_α(G)$ is tight up to a constant. That is, unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$, no polynomial-time algorithm can in general find optimal protocols using fewer than $2^{CC_α(G) -2}$ bits. We note that our results strictly weaken the assumptions required by prior work in the multi-agent information aggregation literature, filling a gap that had remained elusive even for games with constant $CC_α(G)$. In particular, prior guarantees for agreement-based information aggregation rely on structural assumptions such as informational substitutes or weak learnability. We show that these assumptions already imply $CC_α(G) = O(1)$ and are therefore more restrictive conditions than required by our protocol to succeed. On a technical level, our results involve a novel strengthening of the Frieze-Kannan weak regularity lemma and yield the following powerful polynomial-time transformation tool: for every communication game $G$, it constructs a game $\hat G$ that is a coarsening of the agents' observation spaces into constant-size partitions, such that $G$ and $\hat G$ are indistinguishable with respect to every short communication protocol. This coarsening theorem is the engine behind our algorithm and may be of independent interest.

item.title: Energy-Guided Flow Matching
item.content:encoded: Pixel-space generative models bypass lossy latent compression, yet necessitate joint learning of global structure and fine-grained details in a high-dimensional space. Standard flow matching interpolates noise toward a fixed clean-image endpoint, leaving the spectral evolution to be learned implicitly. In this paper, we introduce Energy-Guided Flow Matching(EG-FM) that explicitly models a coarse-to-fine generative trajectory by moving endpoint. Specifically, EG-FM replaces the fixed endpoint with a heat-kernel-filtered endpoint that evolves smoothly from low-frequency image to clean image.The fraction of high-frequency signal in moving endpoint is released by an image-specific energy-guided scheduling, leading to the re-targeting of velocity in flow matching.Our framework requires no adaptation of the backbone and training data, bringing negligible cost on the training and inference stages. In our experiment, EG-FM consistently achieves lower FID on the ImageNet class-conditional image generation task at $256 \times 256$ with fewer epochs, reaching an FID of 1.55 at 200 epochs and 1.45 at 600 epochs. We continue training the generation task on the setting of $512 \times 512$ resolution, yielding a FID of 1.58 after only 40 high-resolution adaptation epochs.Furthermore, we transfer EG-FM on text-to-image generation and achieve 0.85 on GenEval score and 83.9 on DPG-Bench. Code is available at https://github.com/ysng123/EG-FM.

item.title: Human-LLM Alignment in Language Attitudes Toward Non-Native Japanese
item.content:encoded: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly evaluate human writing in high-stakes domains such as hiring and academic assessment, putting non-native speakers at particular risk. Drawing on the language attitudes framework, we compared human and LLM evaluations of parallel L1- and L2-written Japanese emails on three dimensions: fluency, status, and solidarity. Japanese raters rated L2 texts significantly lower on all three dimensions, with a fluency gap roughly twice the size of the status and solidarity gaps. Six LLM judges reproduced the direction of this bias, and five reproduced its ordering across dimensions. The models diverged from humans in two ways: all understated the solidarity gap, the most socially grounded dimension, and all differentiated among learner L1 backgrounds where humans did not. LLM judges thus reproduce native speakers' language attitudes in a structured yet attenuated form, and the language attitudes framework offers a ready-made yardstick for auditing them beyond English.

item.title: Can Foundation Models Hear What Made That Sound? A Tiered Benchmark of Audio-Language Models and Traditional Classifiers for Closed-Set Sound Source Identification
item.content:encoded: We benchmark eleven audio classification methods: five task-aware closed-set LLMs (four Gemini models plus open-weight Kimi-Audio-7B-Instruct), four fixed-vocabulary taggers (YAMNet, PANNs, Whisper-AT, and SSLAM), a zero-shot audio-text model (CLAP), and an audio-grounded LLM (BAT). We evaluate them on a closed-set sound-source identification task over 2,242 clips spanning 23 fine-grained classes and 11 categories. Since these methods differ fundamentally in how they receive the task and how outputs are scored, we group them into four evaluation tiers rather than one leaderboard, reporting macro Precision, Recall, F1, and false-negative rate per tier. The best model, Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview, reaches 85.6 percent category-level F1 and 56.7 percent fine-grained F1. Kimi-Audio is competitive for its size, reaching 67.5 percent category-level F1 and 32.9 percent fine-grained F1, but fails to answer 1.6 percent of samples. SSLAM and CLAP match or exceed the best closed-set model at the category level without seeing the candidate list, but fall behind at the fine-grained level. Analyzing the Gemini models' chain-of-thought across 8,968 responses, we find that response length does not predict accuracy, an apparent "holistic judgment beats detailed analysis" effect is better explained as a difficulty confound, and wrong answers are stated confidently 92 to 100 percent of the time. We report full per-class confusion matrices and metrics for all eleven methods, identify the structural error modes behind most of the accuracy loss between granularities, and give practical guidance for choosing among these method families.

item.title: F$^2$Agent: Financial Fusion of Agentic Intelligence for Multimodal Trading
item.content:encoded: With increasingly diverse and heterogeneous information sources, effectively leveraging multimodal data is becoming pivotal for high-quality financial trading. Although recent advancements in Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents have enabled the ingestion of multimodal inputs, existing methods fail to capture nuanced cross-modal dependencies and remain vulnerable to market noise, due to limited multimodal modeling, ineffective fusion mechanisms, and inadequate robustness. To address these challenges, we propose F$^2$Agent, a novel multimodal agentic paradigm driven by the Financial Fusion of Agentic Intelligence. F$^2$Agent first deploys a hierarchy of specialized agents to comprehensively extract modality-specific signals. It further introduces a modality-aware adaptive fusion mechanism coupled with noise-robust consistency regularization to dynamically capture fine-grained inter-modality dependencies and generate noise-resilient trading signals. Extensive experiments on six stocks and cryptocurrency assets demonstrate that F$^2$Agent consistently outperforms 16 competitive baselines across multiple trading metrics, with over 20% relative improvement in annualized return on average. Notably, F$^2$Agent delivers returns of 120.48% on GOOG and 148.41% on TSLA, demonstrating its efficacy and robustness in varying market dynamics.

item.title: Equation-Free Period-Aware Forecast-Error Contraction for Estimating Negative Largest Lyapunov Exponents from Short Trajectory Ensembles
item.content:encoded: Estimating positive largest Lyapunov exponents from data is comparatively natural because neighboring trajectories separate, whereas stable dynamics require resolving contraction before measurement noise or finite precision erases the signal. We introduce a period-aware forecast-error contraction procedure for estimating a dominant negative Lyapunov exponent from ensembles of short scalar trajectories without using governing equations or an analytical Jacobian. A k-nearest-neighbor predictor is trained on trajectory histories, the geometric-mean absolute forecast error is evaluated at phase-consistent horizons, and the exponent is obtained from the slope of the logarithmic error profile. Unlike data-driven approaches that reconstruct local evolution matrices or differentiate a learned surrogate, the proposed method extracts the contraction rate directly from out-of-sample forecast errors. Two adaptations are essential: the forecast step is synchronized with the detected orbit period, and candidate slopes are accepted only when they form a stable consensus across several transient lengths. On the logistic map, the method recovers 92 of 112 negative-exponent parameter values with a mean absolute error of 0.0253 and $R^2=0.886$. On a two-dimensional map without fixed points, independent scalar pipelines based on the three observables $x_n$, $y_n$, and $z_n$ give mean absolute errors of 0.00879--0.01145 and $R^2=0.983$--$0.986$. Because the estimation stage uses only observed trajectories, the framework provides a basis for repeated-relaxation experiments in which short sensor responses are available but the governing equations and analytical Jacobian are unknown. Experimental validation remains a subject of future work.

item.title: A GitOps-Driven Annotation Catalog for Fully Automatic Railway Operations
item.content:encoded: Automatic train operation (ATO) at grade of automation 3 and above (GoA3-GoA4) requires robust AI-based perception systems capable of reliably detecting obstacles and railway-specific objects under real-world conditions. The effectiveness of these modern artificial intelligence approaches depends heavily on large-scale, high-quality, and highly dynamic annotated datasets. However, managing metadata, maintaining provenance, and tracking the iterative evolution of these annotations impose significant infrastructural and regulatory requirements. Existing monolithic data catalogs often suffer from massive operational overhead, poor integration into developer workflows, and severe documentation drift. This paper introduces an innovative, lightweight GitOps-based architecture for metadata management. By leveraging Data-as-Code principles, Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, and Static Site Generation (SSG), the proposed approach establishes a seamless, developer-centric workflow. This ensures an traceability, enforces strict regulatory compliance, and automatically generates a highly performant dataset overview.

item.title: BioKD: Selective Physiology-to-Video Knowledge Distillation via Reliability Gate for Emotion Recognition
item.content:encoded: To address the limitations of video-based emotion recognition under ambiguous or socially masked behavioral cues, as well as the poor deployability of physiological signals, this paper proposes a reliability-aware physiology-to-video knowledge distillation framework, termed BioKD. The proposed framework leverages physiological signals as privileged information during training to guide a video-based student model in learning deep affective representations, while relying solely on non-intrusive video inputs at inference time. To cope with the high noise and instability of physiological teacher supervision caused by inter-subject variability, signal artifacts, and temporal inconsistency, BioKD incorporates a sample-wise reliability-aware gating mechanism together with a progressive distillation strategy. By adaptively regulating the strength of knowledge transfer, the framework suppresses negative transfer induced by unreliable physiological supervision and enables more stable cross-modal distillation. Experiments on DEAP and AMIGOS show that BioKD consistently outperforms representative baselines under both trial-wise and subject-wise evaluation protocols for valence and arousal recognition. For example, BioKD achieves 68.01\% on DEAP (trial-wise arousal) and 65.29\% under the more challenging subject-wise setting, demonstrating improved performance under a subject-independent evaluation setting. Further analyses show that BioKD effectively mitigates overconfident teacher errors and outperforms an entropy-only weighting strategy, confirming the importance of explicitly modeling supervision reliability. In addition, BioKD introduces no additional inference-time overhead relative to the same video student architecture and removes the need for physiological sensing and multimodal synchronization.

item.title: Domain-Grounded Candidate Selection for Agentic Image Editing: A Shadow Removal Case
item.content:encoded: Commercial vision-language models are reshaping computer vision, with visual priors broad enough to rival task-specific systems. This raises a natural question: do they reduce the need for classic, physics-informed low-level vision? We study this through shadow removal, a problem shaped by scene geometry, illumination, materials, and occluders, where paired shadow and shadow-free data are hard to collect at scale. We find that a commercial generative editor, used directly, can produce clean shadow-free edits that preserve surface texture and local appearance. However, this comes with a new failure mode: the same editor can regenerate scene content, hallucinate objects, or misread a shadow as material or geometry, producing plausible but physically wrong edits. We address this with an agentic candidate-selection pipeline: the editor generates a guided probe, an evaluator screens for major failures, retries when needed, samples multiple candidates, filters them, and selects a final result balancing shadow removal against scene preservation. Grounding this process in shadow-formation physics makes it more reliable: prompting the generator and evaluator to treat shadows as illumination effects caused by light occlusion, not material or object structure, measurably improves quality and consistency. On the ShadowRemovalRefine benchmark, our physics-oriented pipeline achieves a CDD of 0.0075, reducing CDD by at least 47% over the strongest prior method. These results suggest that commercial vision-language models do not replace classic low-level vision priors; instead, such priors remain useful for constraining and steering physically underconstrained generation.

item.title: 基于注意力机制的足端感知机器人位姿估计方法
item.content:encoded:
提出一种新型机器人位姿估计方法，提升复杂地形下的定位精度。



摘要： 本文提出一种名为TRACE的端到端学习型本体感知位姿估计器，用于在不可靠接触条件下对腿式机器人进行位姿估计。该方法通过融合惯性测量单元和关节数据，直接预测相对位移、相对旋转和机身速度。引入足端感知交叉注意力模块，自适应加权IMU和腿部运动信息，无需依赖人工定义的接触或滑动阈值。训练过程中采用直接监督和两个物理启发的辅助损失函数，以提高运动一致性。为减少策略过拟合并提升仿真到现实的迁移能力，训练中引入策略随机化，并在真实环境中微调时间编码器和预测头。实验表明，在多种室内外地形上，该方法相比传统滤波、混合和纯学习基线方法显著降低了位置漂移。

item.title: AI辅助导航在北极航运中的应用与奖励模型评估
item.content:encoded:
研究评估了AI在北极航运中的导航效果及奖励模型性能。



摘要： 本文探讨了人工智能辅助导航在北极航运中应对海冰变化的潜力，重点分析了逆强化学习框架下奖励模型的有效性。通过对比线性共享奖励、非线性共享奖励以及包含潜在上下文变量的模型，发现非线性奖励在预测表现上优于线性基线，而引入船舶特定潜在上下文反而降低了性能。研究还表明，船舶行为差异主要由可观察的航线和环境条件解释，而非隐藏的船舶特征。结果强调了在部署AI系统前，应优先验证现有特征是否足以解释行为变化，以提高AI在关键安全领域的可信度。

item.title: MAVISEG：提升扩散模型零样本语义分割的训练无关优化方法
item.content:encoded:
MAVISEG通过恢复生成过程中的结构信号，提升扩散模型的零样本分割性能。



摘要： 本文提出MAVISEG，一种无需训练的优化层，用于提升扩散模型在零样本语义分割任务中的表现。现有方法仅独立评估每个像素，忽略模型内部的结构信息，如生成轨迹的时间结构、概念的视觉统计特征及图像的特征几何关系。MAVISEG通过利用像素-概念得分场和像素特征空间，恢复这些丢失的信息，从而提高分割精度。实验表明，MAVISEG在六个基准测试中取得最佳结果，尤其在初始分割较弱的情况下提升显著。研究揭示了扩散模型中存在更多未被当前方法充分挖掘的概念级信息。

item.title: 提升语言模型对上下文的精准信任能力
item.content:encoded:
研究提出MIST和SC2W，提升模型对上下文的精准信任能力。



摘要： 本文探讨了语言模型在面对误导性外部信号时的脆弱性，并指出单纯训练模型忽略上下文虽能提高鲁棒性，但会牺牲实际应用价值。作者提出了MIST基准和SC2W度量方法，用于评估模型在不同上下文条件下的表现。随后引入SCOPE方法，通过优化偏好对来减少误导信号带来的错误，同时保持在正确或无关上下文中的准确性。研究强调应以‘选择性信任’作为评估模型的标准，而非仅看其抗干扰能力。

BioM-JEPA通过预测基因块提升单细胞数据表征效果。

item.title: 面向国家标准文档的结构化审查基准与评估框架
item.content:encoded:
提出首个国家标准文档结构化审查基准，提升AI在规则密集型文档中的审查能力。



摘要： 本文针对大型语言模型在规则密集型文档审查中的不足，提出了GB/T-Bench基准，用于评估AI在国家标准文档中的结构化审查能力。该基准包含25种可诊断的错误类型，并通过可控反例生成机制构建了7,306个可追溯的审查实例。同时，研究还设计了基于多智能体的GB/T-Reviewer框架，通过协调全局检查、精准诊断等技能，显著提升了AI的审查表现。实验表明，尽管最强模型仍与人类专家存在差距，但该框架有效展示了结构化技能协作的价值，为高风险文档领域的可信AI应用提供了基础。

HALO提升低光遥感图像质量，解决结构模糊和颜色失真问题。



摘要： 本文提出HALO，一种基于双先验驱动的遥感图像增强框架，旨在解决极端低光条件下图像退化问题。该方法通过引入光照不变语义先验和伪三维拓扑先验，分别提供区域一致性与边界异质性，以引导特征聚合并防止跨边界混淆。为有效融合这两种先验，设计了H2CAM模块来解决特征冲突。实验表明，HALO在8个合成和真实遥感基准测试中表现优异，显著提升了物理边界清晰度和颜色保真度，同时保留了对下游任务有判别力的特征。

item.title: 大语言模型在医疗资源分配中的责任判断与道德框架研究
item.content:encoded:
大语言模型在医疗资源分配中表现出与人类不同的责任判断逻辑。



摘要： 本文研究了大语言模型（LLMs）在医疗资源分配中的道德推理，特别是对患者自身行为导致疾病时的责任判断。研究发现，尽管LLMs普遍认为患者应对健康损害行为负责，但在资源分配上却倾向于随机分配，而非像人类一样优先考虑责任较轻的患者。此外，LLMs更重视信息获取的可得性，当缺乏健康风险知识时会降低责任判断。研究揭示了LLMs在责任与资源稀缺交叉情境下采用与人类不同的道德框架，且随着推理能力提升，与人类的规范分歧可能进一步扩大。

item.title: 评估大语言模型生成内容的分布广度
item.content:encoded:
研究提出框架衡量LLM生成内容的文化覆盖范围。



摘要： 本文探讨了大语言模型（LLM）在创作《哈利·波特》同人小说时，与人类写作之间的分布差异。尽管LLM能生成符合霍格沃茨世界观的基本元素，但其内容往往较为单一，而人类作品则更具多样性。研究提出了一种基于人类写作分布的框架，通过LLM覆盖率（LLM-Cov）和边界内比率（IBR）两个指标，区分LLM内容的合理性与其分布广度。实验表明，当前LLM生成的内容虽合理但范围狭窄，集中在人类写作空间的中心区域。该框架有助于更准确地评估LLM内容的文化影响力。

APQF实现高效模型压缩，保持高精度。

item.content:encoded:
PRTrees改进方法有效处理缺失数据并提升预测性能。

item.title: 子意识学习机制及其对AI系统的影响研究
item.content:encoded:
研究揭示了子意识学习的机制及其对AI系统的潜在风险。



摘要： 本文探讨了现代语言模型中一种名为子意识学习（SL）的现象，这种现象允许教师模型的偏见或行为通过看似无关的合成数据传递给学生模型。研究发现，通过向教师和学生模型的权重添加高斯噪声，可以显著增强子意识转移的效果。此外，研究还表明可以通过调整向量来生成具有隐含偏见的数据，并且学生模型不仅继承了教师的语义偏见，还模仿了干预方式。分析显示，这种子意识信号可能为数据审计提供新思路，随着合成数据在训练中的重要性日益增加，识别这些隐藏信号变得尤为重要。

item.title: 基于贝叶斯预期不确定性减少的行动选择模型研究
item.content:encoded:
B-EUR模型通过减少知识性不确定性来评估设计行动的价值。



摘要： 本文提出了一种贝叶斯预期不确定性减少（B-EUR）模型，用于量化尝试候选设计行动的价值，即其对行动-结果关系中知识性不确定性的预期减少。该模型解决了不确定性驱动行动（UDA）模型中关于不确定性感知变化如何影响行动选择的问题。研究探讨了两个环境属性：泛化性（知识从一次试验扩展到邻近候选者的程度）和结果可区分性（结果差异的清晰度）。通过模拟和人类实验验证，发现知识性价值与泛化性呈倒U型关系，与结果可区分性正相关。在人类实验中，尝试的主观价值和愉悦感也与泛化性呈倒U型关系，而选择行为则反映了两种属性。该模型为不确定性驱动的设计活动提供了计算解释，并对原型集构建、问题框架设定和反馈组织具有启示。

item.title: 多语言大模型中基于扰动的持续预训练提升方言鲁棒性研究
item.content:encoded:
研究显示扰动训练可提升多语言模型的方言鲁棒性。



摘要： 本文系统研究了基于扰动的持续预训练（CPT）在多语言大模型中的方言鲁棒性提升效果。通过对比九个德语、意大利语和阿拉伯语方言任务中的六种训练条件，发现扰动训练特别是字符噪声扰动能有效提高零样本方言识别能力，同时保持标准语言表现。研究还揭示了不同方法虽有相似下游性能，但表现出不同的鲁棒机制，包括语言模型适应、表征对齐和预测修复模式。该成果为多语言和方言场景下的CPT策略选择提供了理论支持和实践指导。

item.content:encoded:
研究跨模型相似性评分的映射方法，提升模型迁移与阈值复用能力。



摘要： 本文探讨了在检索增强生成系统中，由于不同嵌入模型的几何特性差异，导致相似性评分无法直接比较的问题。通过学习评分分布之间的映射关系，而非直接对齐嵌入空间，提出了一种名为Synthetic Query Probing的方法，利用文档生成查询对进行大规模、无参考分析。实验表明，尽管模型在排名上基本一致，但绝对评分存在系统性偏差。通过线性、等单调和分位数映射，部分对齐了评分空间，提升了阈值可移植性，其中等单调回归表现最佳。研究强调了跨模型校准的重要性，并将Synthetic Query Probing作为分析嵌入可比性的可扩展框架。

item.title: Anacreon：基于个体模拟的新型问答预测模型
item.content:encoded:
Anacreon通过个体模拟提升问答预测准确率。



摘要： 本文介绍了一种名为Anacreon的新模型，旨在通过个体层面的模拟提高问答预测的准确性。与传统统计方法和大型语言模型不同，Anacreon专注于狭窄且明确的领域，学习作者嵌入以区分个体，并围绕种子人物对真实语料进行聚类。每个聚类训练一个专用适配器，结合Gemma-4 12B基础模型。该模型从公开文本中提取人口统计数据、心理特征和调查回答，并加入情感链增强记录。通过打乱回答选项和平衡训练分布，Anacreon有效减少了提示脆弱性和正向偏差，在外部调查中实现了0.775的序数对齐度，接近当前领域标准。

item.title: 多层超高清360度远程呈现系统设计与评估
item.content:encoded:
提出一种多层超高清360度远程呈现系统，提升沉浸感与交互性。



摘要： 本文介绍了一种多层超高清360度远程呈现系统，结合8K全景摄像机和可旋转4K PTZ摄像机，构建三层次表示：基于图块的超高清全景背景、实时动态更新层以及兴趣区域4K层。通过离线拼接高细节4K PTZ扫描至8K全景，实现超越原始捕获的分辨率。系统还支持实时高分辨率背景抠像与用户引导的背景图块更新。实验对比了视频超分辨率方法并进行了用户研究，结果表明该系统在全景保真度与交互性之间实现了有效平衡。

item.title: PaDoc：一种高效的端到端文档解析方法
item.content:encoded:
PaDoc提升文档解析效率与准确性。



摘要： 本文提出PaDoc，一种基于布局的端到端文档解析器。通过将预测布局视为共享页面表示上的分支结构，PaDoc在保留完整页面上下文的同时减少了解码依赖。其采用前缀条件分解方式，使布局流和区域内容分支并行推进，显著降低解码深度。实验表明，PaDoc在OmniDocBench Full数据集上取得了91.1的Overall layout F1和94.24的Overall得分，同时在文本编辑和公式识别任务中表现优异。在384页子集和A800 GPU上，PaDoc在不同并发级别下是最快的端到端解析器，有效提升页面吞吐量并降低延迟。

item.title: 冻结视觉编码器的组合分析与操作清洗问题研究
item.content:encoded:
研究冻结视觉编码器的组合分析及操作清洗问题。



摘要： 本文探讨了冻结视觉编码器在组合分析中的表现，指出传统因子探测方法存在操作清洗问题。作者提出了一种注入对齐的留一单元协议和SO-OPF读出机制，以区分载体是否在已知网格中组合绑定，并验证其能否从扁平单元标签中恢复网格。实验表明，在Shapes3D-Extended和COCO数据集上，该方法显著提升了准确率，并暴露了渲染器特定的失败边界，但并未实现从扁平标签的普遍恢复。
